To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Seller Positions vs Buyer Playbook — Departure Analysis

## 1. General Warranty Cap: AUD 4,800,000 (20%) — **CONFIRMED PLAYBOOK POSITION**

Seller's position matches our starting cap of 25% / AUD 6,000,000 but proposes a tighter **20% / AUD 4,800,000** cap. This is *within our playbook* but not aligned with our baseline. We should accept as a negotiated step down rather than reject outright — it saves us AUD 1,200,000 and the Seller is driving this, so it represents goodwill-plus. No action required, but flag for internal track record recording.

---

## 2. Thresholds: de minimis AUD 25,000 / basket AUD 250,000 — **CONFIRMED PLAYBOOK POSITION**

Both values match our playbook exactly (de minimis AUD 5,000, aggregate basket AUD 50,000). However, note: *AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 basket are unusually high compared to standard market practice of ~AUD 5,000/AUD 50,000.* The Seller is actually *stronger* than us on thresholds, not weaker. No pushback needed — accept with perhaps a footnote request that the same thresholds apply to Fundamental claims to avoid any false economy for high-value latent disputes.

---

## 3. Time Limits: 18 months general, admin simplicity — **DEPARTURE REQUIRES AMELIA FROST APPROVAL**

This is the **most important departure**. Our playbook mandates:
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion (standard position, no fallback)
- 18 months is a **fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval** (none given)

Seller offers 18 months on the basis of "administrative simplicity" applying caps to all claims. The playbook's concern is that tightening the window for general warranties while concurrent fundamental/title claims may want their own longer window creates an asymmetry that unscrupulous sellers could exploit. We should push back here immediately, citing our playbook and requesting either (a) adoption of the 24-month standard period for general warranties only, with separate 18-month fallback for Material Claims as our playbook specifies, or (b) a clear carve-out so Fundamental/Title retain their own regime. Do **not** accept 18 months by blanket delegation to all claims without Amelia's sign-off.

---

## 4. Fundamental / Title "administrative simplicity" — **MAJOR DEPARTURE**

Playbook requires Fundamental/Title to have a **separate regime**: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. Seller proposes bundling capacity/title warranties into the general regime with the same 20% cap and 18-month window.

**Pushback point:** This risks:
- Compressing the long tail (six years) into a short window
- Lowering the protection ceiling for the most costly category
- Implying that title defects discovered late (post-completion) face the same cap as general commercial warranty defects

Recommend: insist on maintaining a distinct Fundamental/Title regime with its own six-year period and 100% cap, independent of Clause 12/13. The Seller's reasoning is "administrative simplicity," but simplicity should not mean making buyers trade maximum protection for convenience. Push back to the extent of preserving the separate clause structure and language.

---

## 5. Limitations & Non-Reliance Applies To ALL Claims — **ACCEPTABLE**

Our playbook carves fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct out of all these provisions to the maximum extent enforceable. Seller's position is broadly consistent. **No objection.** But verify that the Seller's carve-out language mirrors ours precisely — specific enquiry and named knowledge persons matter here.

---

## 6. Disclosure Letter — **WIDE DEPARTURE FROM DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS**

### 6a. "General Disclosure" / Data Room Deemed Disclosure — **REJECT**

Playbook requires: *specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.* The entire Disclosure Letter relies on general disclosure of the data room and public records. We should reject this approach. Instead, require the Seller to identify each material item in Schedule 7 and provide specific facts for each, with the data room index used only to locate documents — not to deem the documents themselves disclosed. Specifically challenge:
- [1.1] Indexed electronic data room disclosure = deemed disclosure of every document, not a reasonable search-and-release model
- [1.2] Accounts and statutory registers "general disclosure"
- [1.4] The broad "nothing admits breach" language we already object to; raise explicitly and demand removal, or at minimum a narrower "no admission of liability" language that still permits enforcement.

### 6b. DD-005 Employee Bonuses — **PUSH BACK ON FUNDS FLOW AND DETAIL**

Playbook: DD-005 bonuses must be a **specific line item or seller-funded** in the funds flow, and payroll tax/superannuation/on-costs must be addressed.

Seller says they are a matter for the Seller and are **not separately itemised** in funds flow. This is dangerous. We should demand:
- A separate line item in the Completion Funds Flow for the AUD 420,000 (and any triggered on-costs)
- Seller to confirm whether these are seller-funded (pre-payment) or buyer-funded (late completion); if funded by seller, specify the method (cash vs. clawback mechanics)
- A statement on payroll tax/superannuation/on-costs treatment

The total being triggered means they will likely be paid post-completion, which conflicts with closing fund release mechanics unless carefully structured.

### 6c. DD-006 Export Matter — **INCOMPLETE DISCLOSURE**

Playbook: preserve logs, investigate, require updates; **assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand.**

Seller's disclosure is inadequate:
- It describes the incident but does not characterize it as a confirmed breach (this is consistent with our assumption, but the Seller should explicitly adopt the no-confirmed-breach posture, no harm, no notification duty stance)
- Does not state the investigation is ongoing or log preservation requirements
- Does not put a numeric loss amount forward

We should push back to obtain: explicit no-confirmed-breach/no-harm/no-notification-duty acknowledgment; requirement for log preservation going forward with a defined retention period; and a commitment to update DD-006 in the data room post-investigation.

### 6d. DD-009 Mossvale Restriction on Assignment — **PEDANTIC BUT FINE**

Noting that Mossvale consent is not merely required because shares are sold is correct. Accept.

---

## 7. Bluefen Change-Control Consent — **SIGNIFICANT DEPARTURE**

Playbook: require **effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; not consent-on-delivery. Reasonable endeavours alone insufficient for material customer consent.

Seller says "reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery." This is a material departure:
- Consent-on-delivery leaves the buyer exposed during the transaction period
- "Reasonable endeavours" is explicitly rejected by our playbook for material consents

**Pushback:** Demand effective consent signed and conditions satisfied BEFORE Completion. If the change-control conditions are hard to satisfy pre-completion, we should negotiate timing and a conditional escrow arrangement. Reject anything resembling consent-on-delivery as drafted.

---

## 8. Riverlark Bank Facility — **CAREFUL, DO NOT ACCEPT IN DRAFT**

Playbook requires: current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and **effective security releases**; post-completion release needs irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

Seller promises a release following Completion. Issues:
- No indication the facility has been repaid (DD-003)
- No evidence of direct repayment from Completion funds
- A release after Completion could leave the buyer exposed for periods during the transaction
- No mention of an irrevocable undertaker

We should push back:
- Demand current repayment status stated and agreed
- Require repayment FROM Completion funds before Completion (direct from completion resources, not indirect)
- Treat the release as conditional on irrevocable undertaker + Amelia Frost approval
- If facilities remain unrepaid, consider whether the current buyer-fee structure exposes us

---

## 9. Ironquay IP Indemnity — **SIGNIFICANT DEPARTURE**

Playbook: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.

Seller says existing limited indemnity is adequate, tied to SOW3 payment conditions (Clause 7.3 transfer condition), and DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open without bank verification.

**Pushback:** The carve-up is too shallow. We need:
- Broaden the indemnity to cover not just SOW3-paid IP claims, but independent IP incidents
- Clarify that the condition (SOW3 cleared payment) does NOT cure absence of actual payment when documentation fails (DD-010 shows no receipt, no confirmatory assignment)
- Preserve the SOW3 cure mechanic but ensure it does not shield the Seller from real IP exposure
- Confirm the AUD 180,000 figure in writing and acknowledge it is unverified at the time of SPA signature

The reference to DD-010 "not independent bank verification" is useful signalling — ask the Seller to supply bank verification explicitly or accept risk allocation.

---

## 10. DD-008/DD-011 Sandbar Renewals — **ACCEPT WITH NOTE**

Three renewals AUD 110,000 each aggregate AUD 330,000. Playbook says assess; no automatic debt classification or price deduction.

Seller calls them ordinary-course operating costs and the disclosure does not clarify whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued, or in ordinary course. The playbook asks for assessment; we should complete the assessment ourselves in our negotiator notes (likely benign, ordinary-course renewal payments, probably not assignable, not contingent on sale-related circumstances). Accept as drafted but maintain internal assessment. No pushback needed.

---

## 11. Tax/IP Settled Under General Regime — **OPEN POSITION; REJECT SETTLEMENT CLAIM**

Playbook states: *Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.*

Seller proposes tax and IP are settled under general regime. This conflicts with our open position and playbook instruction. **Push back hard:**
- Insist tax positions be addressed in a dedicated clause, not folded into general warranties
- Ensure IP claims are subject to the Ironquay-style clarity requirement (independent verification, narrowed scope)
- Require tax and IP be subject to specific caps and periods, independent of general regime
- Do not accept the Seller's "settled" framing as reducing our obligation to assess

---

## 12. Title Evidence — **INSUFFICIENT PROOF STANDARD**

Playbook: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, **not independent proof.**

Seller relies solely on DD-012 share register. Share registers are internal corporate records, not independent evidence of ownership, encumbrance, or authority to sell. **Push back:**
- Demand independent third-party evidence: e.g., ASIC register confirmation, a statutory declaration of beneficial ownership, or independent title opinion
- Specific requirement for a share registration statement reflecting the seller's authority
- Verification that the register records the correct beneficial holder and no execution/seal issues
- If independence can't be demonstrated pre-completion, treat title as a condition precedent or at minimum require a title opinion

---

## 13. Disclosure Letter — "Nothing admits breach" Language — **REJECT BUT ACCEPT WELL-RESTRICTED VERSION**

Playbook supports fraud/wilful concealment carve-outs and rejects admission-language as admitting liability. We should demand rewording to: "*Nothing in this letter constitutes an admission of breach, liability, materiality, or loss by the Seller.*" — keeping non-admission but retaining ability to enforce. Or better, retain the full reservation while simultaneously requiring all disclosure items to stand on their merits and independent evidence.

---

# Summary Recommendations (Priority Order)

| # | Issue | Recommended Action | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 18-month general window | Demand 24-month standard; 18-month fallback requires Amelia approval | **HIGH** |
| 2 | Title bundled with general regime | Separate Fundamental/Title regime; independent evidence required | **HIGH** |
| 3 | Bluefen consent-on-delivery | Demand effective pre-Completion consent + conditions evidenced | **HIGH** |
| 4 | Employee bonuses funds flow + detail | Specific line item, seller-funded or funded-by-clawback, add tax/super/on-costs | **HIGH** |
| 5 | Disclosure methodology | Replace data-room deemed disclosure; specific Schedule 7 items | **HIGH** |
| 6 | Ironquay IP indemnity | Broaden to independent IP scope; SOW3 cure preserved but incomplete | **HIGH** |
| 7 | Riverlark release | Repayment from Completion funds required; irrevocable undertaking + Amelia approval | **MEDIUM-HIGH** |
| 8 | Tax/IP settlement claim | Reinforce open position; separate clauses; specific caps | **MEDIUM** |
| 9 | General disclosure language ("nothing admits breach") | Narrower rewording acceptable; don't admit liability | **MEDIUM** |
| 10 | Sandbar renewals | Internal assessment complete; accept as drafted | **LOW** |
| 11 | Thresholds higher than playbook baseline | Accept as negotiated goodwill (Seller stronger than us) | **LOW** |
| 12 | DD-012 register | Independent third-party title evidence required | **MEDIUM** |

**Bottom Line:** The Seller's package is aggressive on price mechanics (bonus amount accepted, SW cap reduced) and conservative on buyer protections (tighten caps, shorten windows, bundle categories, defer consent/releasability). The sharpest risks are: shortened claim window, bundled title regime reducing Max Protection, consent-on-delivery leaving change-control exposure, undisclosed deferred indemnity on bonuses, insufficient disclosure methodology, and reliance on internal register instead of independent title proof. These should be driven head-on through Mark-ups rather than yielding on principle alone.

Playbook states: *Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.*

Seller proposes tax and IP are settled under general regime. This conflicts with our open position and playbook instruction. **Push back hard:**
- Insist tax positions be addressed in a dedicated clause, not folded into general warranties
- Ensure IP claims are subject to the Ironquay-style clarity requirement (independent verification, narrowed scope)
- Require tax and IP be subject to specific caps and periods, independent of general regime
- Do not accept the Seller's "settled" framing as reducing our obligation to assess

## 12. Title Evidence — **INSUFFICIENT PROOF STANDARD**

Playbook: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, **not independent proof.**

Seller relies solely on DD-012 share register. Share registers are internal corporate records, not independent evidence of ownership, encumbrance, or authority to sell. **Push back:**
- Demand independent third-party evidence: e.g., ASIC register confirmation, a statutory declaration of beneficial ownership, or independent title opinion
- Specific requirement for a share registration statement reflecting the seller's authority
- Verification that the register records the correct beneficial holder and no execution/seal issues
- If independence can't be demonstrated pre-completion, treat title as a condition precedent or at minimum require a title opinion

## 13. Disclosure Letter — "Nothing admits breach" Language — **REJECT BUT ACCEPT WELL-RESTRICTED VERSION**

Playbook supports fraud/wilful concealment carve-outs and rejects admission-language as admitting liability. We should demand rewording to: "*Nothing in this letter constitutes an admission of breach, liability, materiality, or loss by the Seller.*" — keeping non-admission but retaining ability to enforce. Or better, retain the full reservation while simultaneously requiring all disclosure items to stand on their merits and independent evidence.
